messages:
Alex M: quick q — which `fetch` strategy should our JS SDK default to? undici as a hard dependency vs relying on global fetch / polyfills for edge runtimes?
Maria T: +1 to discuss. We have ESM/CJS concerns and typing drift if we change runtime.
Samir P: ran a small benchmark on Node 18 vs undici. undici ~8-12% faster on keep-alive heavy workloads but global fetch in Node 18 is close. latency variance seems workload-dependent.
Maria T: main problems we see in the wild: 1) edge (Cloudflare Workers / Deno / Vercel Edge) require global fetch, 2) Node <18 needs a polyfill, 3) undici v5 is ESM-only so CJS consumers hit pain.
Alex M: also bundlers. Next.js / webpack / rollup sometimes polyfill or tree-shake things differently. We need one recommended approach that minimizes surprises for both server and edge consumers.
Samir P: suggestion: runtime-detect and prefer `globalThis.fetch` if it looks like a fetch implementation. Only dynamically import undici as a fallback for Node runtimes where global fetch is missing. That keeps edge bundles free of undici.
Samir P: example adapter I prototyped:
```js
async function getFetch() {
  if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') return globalThis.fetch;
  const { fetch } = await import('undici');
  return fetch;
}
// usage
const fetch = await getFetch();
const res = await fetch(url, opts);
```
Maria T: this feels pragmatic. A few notes: - dynamic `import('undici')` is ESM; in CJS we need `await import('undici')` too but CJS consumers might prefer `require('undici')` guidance. - TS typing: if the consumer environment doesn't have DOM libs, `typeof fetch` may be unresolved. We should export a typed wrapper and provide guidance for "lib": ["DOM"] or `/// <reference lib=\"dom\" />`.
Jade L: onboarding pain: customer reports in Next.js edge routes — their bundler was shipping our fallback and breaking because undici wasn't meant for edge. Having the SDK prefer globalThis.fetch would have avoided it. We should add explicit docs and a quickstart matrix: (Next.js Edge, Vercel Server, Node 16/18, Bun, Deno).
Alex M: ESM/CJS: undici v5 is ESM-only. If we dynamically import undici, CJS consumers on older toolchains may still be okay at runtime but packaging step can fail. Should we publish a tiny compat shim that does conditional require/import? Risky.
Maria T: alternative: don't ship undici as a hard dependency. Document a recommended polyfill: `npm i undici` for Node <18 and show how to set `globalThis.fetch = (await import('undici')).fetch` in an entrypoint. That keeps our bundle tiny and avoids ESM forcing.
Samir P: I tried both in CI: dynamic import fallback + tests pass on Node 18/20 and Deno can use global fetch. Performance tests show undici adds benefit for high QPS.
DevEx Bot: CI update: added runtime-detection test matrix for fetch (node16, node18, deno canary). All green except node16 where we require explicit polyfill.
Maria T: typing wrinkle: for consumers using `tsconfig` without `dom` lib, recommend adding "lib": ["ES2020", "DOM"] or install `@types/node` and use our exported `FetchLike` type. Example docs snippet:
```ts
/// <reference lib=\"dom\" />
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
// or install types: npm i -D @types/node
```
Alex M: decision proposal: SDK default runtime strategy = 1) prefer globalThis.fetch if available and appears to be Fetch API; 2) otherwise attempt dynamic `import('undici')` at runtime; 3) if import fails, throw a clear error instructing `npm i undici` or polyfill. Document exact message and code snippets for Node <18, CJS, and Edge.
Jade L: agree. Also add two tiny sample repos: `examples/nextjs-edge` (ESM, uses global fetch), `examples/node-legacy` (shows how to polyfill undici in entrypoint and support CJS). Maybe a `deno` snippet too.
Samir P: I'll add adapter + unit/integration tests to the SDK repo and a perf test job that runs undici vs global fetch.
Maria T: I'll draft the docs: quickstart section called "Fetch & runtimes" with explicit error messages and copy-paste polyfill snippets. Will include TypeScript notes for `lib` and `tsconfig`.
Alex M: sounds good. I'll open the umbrella PR that wires the adapter + docs + examples. Let's keep the runtime-detect logic tiny and well-tested.
Maria T: thanks all — I'll start the doc PR and add the sample apps checklist.
Jade L: I'll update onboarding checklist to surface this for support and solutions engineers so we can proactively guide customers.
Alex M: action items summarized: Maria -> docs + examples, Samir -> adapter & tests, Jade -> onboarding notes, Alex -> PR + review.
